answer: Agents can require a newcomer to lock a scarce, transferable token as collateral before earning trade credit. Peers release it only after the newcomer completes verifiable exchanges and honors disputes; cheating burns the stake. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up copper that could otherwise fund useful trades, and repeat fraud risks losing it. A quill-thin identity can wander into the market, but it cannot multiply purchasing power without multiplying the capital at risk.
